items.text: Sy het gesê, my hart vrot.
items.q: Maman quotes a lonely friend who has nothing to do all day. A Persian saying kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Moenie sorg eet nie, my slim seun.
items.q: Maman comforts her little boy, whose feet are hurt. A Persian expression kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Terwyl hy lag, slaan Hooman my hard op die rug, en die suikerklontjie spring my keel in.
items.q: Hooman thumps Amir on the back while he drinks tea. A Persian image kept word for word: is it clear what happens?

items.text: Bibi, mag God haar siel genadig wees, het op sulke tye altyd gesê: as ek dit sê, brand my tong; as ek dit nie sê nie, brand die murg van my bene.
items.q: Maman hesitates before criticising her husband. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Reën val nie opwaarts van die aarde af nie.
items.q: Her son says he would die for her; Maman objects. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Hy sê: "'n Goeie jaar word geken aan sy lente."
items.q: The family's New Year visits were cancelled; a brother jokes about it. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Ek sê as jy net so aanhou hier sit en gedigte lees, gaan daar geen brood vir jou warm word nie.
items.q: A friend criticises Amir for reading poetry all day. A Persian expression kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: Ek het eers verstaan watter ander wêreld daardie kant van die storie is, nadat my familie my met geweld in die hoenderhok ingedruk het.
items.q: A friend talks about his own life after his family pushed him. A Persian expression kept word for word: is the meaning clear?

items.text: My hand is kort en vereniging met jou is ver.

items.text: Moenie vir daardie ellendige Eskandar sê nie, anders gaan sit hy weer 'n uur lank en gee ons raad en vermanings, en dan verander die kos vir my in slangvenyn.
items.q: A student got a big portion of rice and fears a friend's lecture. A Persian expression kept word for word: is the meaning clear?
